chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said:
"The blind slave, the one with a missing limb (amputee), and the insane person are valid for expiations (kaffarat), because the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) freed them."

key_terms.الْأَجْذَمُ: The amputee (one with a missing limb)
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَاتِ: Expiations (penalties or compensations for specific acts or omissions)

ai.seo_question: Are blind or insane slaves valid for performing kaffarat (expiation)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that slaves who are blind, amputated, or insane are eligible to fulfill their manumission as expiation (*kaffarat*), grounded in the Prophetic precedent of freeing such individuals. It highlights the Shia juristic view that physical or mental disabilities do not invalidate the slave's capacity to serve as the object of redemption, reflecting the Prophet's practice of liberating those with specific impairments.
